physics_reverification.method: Re-derived from src/core/formulas.py from scratch, independent of rounds 4 and 5.
detail: FIG 1 (phononic, p.3): diatomic_branches(1,2,1,k) matches 3/2 +- sqrt(5/4 + cos k) to 4.44e-16 max error over 20001 k-samples; acoustic max = 1.000000000000 and optical min = 2.000000000000, so BOTH gap edges are attained (tight, not loose); ZERO states strictly inside (1,2); phononic_gap_edges() = (1.0, 2.0); the printed rational inner bracket 1 < 141/100 <= sqrt(2) = 1.4142135624 holds.

FIG 2 (PT/EP, p.4): Delta = 2 sqrt(1 - g^2) = 0.200000000000000 exactly at g^2 = 99/100, so the printed 'Delta <= 1/5 (tight)' enclosure is genuinely tight; Delta = 0 at g = 1 (EP2 defective). Re lambda for g <= 1 and Im lambda for g > 1 on one axis is the standard PT convention, named per trace in the legend and stated in the caption.

FIG 3 as printed (effective medium, p.5): maxwell_garnett(1,4,f) = 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.0 at f = 0 / 1/2 / 1, so the certified point is exact and the non-strict constituent bounds are attained at both endpoints; eps in [1,4] over 4001 samples; Voigt >= Reuss on every sample; at f = 2/3 Voigt = 3.000000000000, Reuss = 2.000000000000, voigt_reuss_gap = 1.000000000000, matching the closed form f(1-f)(M1-M2)^2/((1-f)M2 + f M1) = 1.000000000000.

FIG 4 as printed (Haldane, p.6): haldane_mass_inversion_window(1, pi/2) = 5.196152422706632 = 3 sqrt(3) exactly; haldane_dirac_masses gives opposite-sign cone masses at m = 1 (-4.196, +6.196) and at m = 5 (-0.196, +10.196), and SAME-sign at m = 6 (+0.804, +11.196). m = 5 is inside the window (5 < 5.196) with inverted masses yet reads C = 0 — the counterexample the figure is built on is real, not an artefact of the plot.

cross_cutting.finding: The ADVISORY drift half of bundle_figure_integrity is DEAD CODE and reports a false negative. validate.py:2167 calls pathlib.Path(tmp_path), but validate.py imports 'from pathlib import Path' (line 70) and has NO module-level name 'pathlib'. Every iteration therefore raises NameError: name 'pathlib' is not defined before it can compare hashes, and the bare 'except Exception: pass' at lines 2176-2177 swallows it silently. PROVEN two ways: (a) replaying the exact block in validate.py's own module namespace raises NameError: name 'pathlib' is not defined; (b) behaviourally — a mutation that changed a figure's title, guaranteeing a different render, produced NO drift warning for any of the 7 figures. The reported 'zero drift' is therefore not evidence of zero drift; the comparison never executes. Same self-concealing-guard pattern as the round-4 F3 defect, one level up: the guard exists, is wired, runs, and cannot fire.
cross_cutting.why_not_blocking: (1) The drift detail is warning-only by design, so even working it could not change the check's pass/fail — the binding half is unaffected. (2) Drift verified independently: all four D11 PNGs are byte-identical by sha256 to a fresh fig.write_image(scale=3) render at identical dimensions (canvases 800x420, 800x420, 900x430, 880x470; PNGs 2400x1260, 2400x1260, 2700x1290, 2640x1410). The reviewed PDF provably reflects current source. R5-7 (output_dir) is subsumed here: the intended answer was built, it just does not execute yet.
cross_cutting.recommendation: One-token fix: use Path(tmp_path) (already imported at line 70), or add pathlib to the inner 'import hashlib, tempfile, os as _os' line. Separately, narrow the bare 'except Exception: pass' to the renderer errors it is meant to tolerate, or emit a warning-severity Detail when the comparison could not be performed — a guard that cannot distinguish 'no drift' from 'did not run' is the exact failure mode this check was added to end.
cross_cutting.section_ref: scripts/validate.py, check_bundle_figure_integrity(), the advisory drift block — the line `fresh = hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(tmp_path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()` (line 2167 when first read at 23:12, line 2175 at 23:47 after a concurrent edit shifted the file; the block itself is byte-identical). `from pathlib import Path` is at line 70/72; there is no module-level name `pathlib`.

summary: Round 6 is a scoped confirmation pass and every item confirms. R5-8, the single blocking item and a prose defect rather than a figure one, is genuinely fixed: 0 Overfull hbox (was 1), and independently of the log, page 2 now shows a 17.93 pt clear gutter with zero same-line column collisions across all 8 pages; at 600 dpi the theorem name wraps as sum_plaquetteArg_eq_two_pi_mul_ / latticeChern with the underscore printed at the break, so it reconstructs unambiguously, and the right column's 'not' is fully intact. R5-6 is confirmed to be a real, binding gate: four independent mutations — per-trace textfont, canvas width, axis title font, tickfont — each correctly FAIL it, and two of those fields were invisible to the round-4 helper, so the systemic F3 class is now prevented rather than merely fixed. R5-2 and R5-5 confirm fixed as stated, and the 508 pt constant now tracks my raster measurement to within 0.01 pt. Physics re-derived from formulas.py from scratch is correct in all four figures, and all three anchors pass — the highest-priority one on a 53-string sweep, a caption sweep, a structural check (four single-point traces, no C(m) curve) and a semantic reading (the figure refutes the continuum picture rather than implying it). One new harness MINOR: the gate's ADVISORY drift half is dead code — a NameError on pathlib, swallowed by a bare except — so its 'zero drift' cannot be distinguished from 'never ran'; it is not blocking because that half is warning-only and because byte-identity of all four shipped PNGs against fresh renders was verified independently. What remains is six MINORs, all accepted-class: three carried from round 5 by the operator's own triage, one new cosmetic label/line contact, and two harness gaps that do not touch the printed paper.
